title: The unity and diversity of social cognition subdomains in adults: A latent variable analysis.
abstract: Social cognition has been postulated to comprise three subdomains: perception, understanding, and regulation. However, empirical research into the factor structure of social cognition is limited. This hampers theoretical understanding and the development of sensitive neuropsychological measures for clinical application. The primary objective of the present study was to examine the extent to which the three postulated social cognition subdomains are unified or distinct based on currently available measures. In this cross-sectional study, 201 healthy adults (mean age = 43.4 years, SD = 18.9) completed up to 10 social cognition measures. The structure of social cognition was investigated by fitting six confirmatory factor analysis models that assumed varying degrees of unity. Model comparisons revealed that a two-factor model distinguishing perception and a combined understanding-regulation factor fitted the data best relative to model complexity. The secondary objective was to examine the contributions of the observed factors to performance on a serious game designed to measure theory of mind. In a subsample (n = 68), four latent regression path models were fitted. The model with a single path from the combined understanding-regulation factor to the serious game provided the best fit relative to model complexity. The primary findings suggest that social cognition comprises at least two highly related yet partially distinct subdomains. These findings are consistent with a distinct perception subdomain, but indicate that the assigned measures did not form a distinct regulation factor, which may reflect measurement limitations, the breadth of the regulation construct, or regulation not being a separable subdomain.
